_comment: A street map of the few blocks round one address, drawn from OpenStreetMap by scripts/place-map.py: land, buildings, parks, water and streets, with no lettering and no pin -- the film letters the real street names (the data sheet says where each runs) and drops its own pin, in its own look. Sizes are METRES on the ground, so a street keeps its real width at any scale; min_px keeps the thin ones visible. A tone is a whole palette; a film's tint moves each surface toward its own colour by the fraction in `tint`, and `colors` in a spec replaces any surface outright.

tint._comment: how far each surface moves toward a film's tint colour (0 = the tone's own). The tint is first made as light as the surface it tints, so it changes the hue and never the lightness

roads._comment: drawn in this order, every casing first; w_m and case_m in metres. skip: ways never drawn (a driveway and a parking aisle per house turn a neighbourhood to hatching; a sidewalk mapped as its own way doubles every street)

labels._comment: where each street's name is lettered: n streets at most (the pin's own first, then the larger and the nearer), each on a straight stretch about `ring` of the map's width from the pin (the pin's own street nearer, at own_ring) and long enough to hold the name (`char` of the width a letter), `apart` of the width clear of every other name and of the pin, `margin` from the edge; alt: spare spots a street, alt_apart of the width from each other
